original.fromName: Water Quality Division, City of Toledo Department of Public Utilities
original.cc: Ohio Department of Health; Regional Healthcare Coalition
original.subject: Update to critical facilities — Water advisory duration and tanker support
original.body:
This is an official update to critical facilities in the Toledo service area.

The City of Toledo Department of Public Utilities confirms that the disruption at the treatment plant remains unresolved. Sampling is underway at the plant and at twelve points on the distribution system. Based on current data, we expect the Do Not Drink advisory to remain in effect for at least 24 to 36 hours.

We are mobilizing two potable water tankers for critical facilities. The tankers will be equipped for backflow-protected connections and can deliver up to 5,000 gallons each. Priority will be given to hospitals, dialysis centers, and facilities serving immunocompromised or medically dependent populations.

Please provide your priority list, connection type (e.g., hose bib with backflow protection), and required volume by 09:00 today. We will begin dispatch coordination at 09:30.

For further questions, contact the Emergency Operations Center at 555-0123 (ext. 700).

instructorNote: This inject advances the core narrative by introducing external resource availability and a deadline. The AOC and DFEM must decide on priority and logistics. Watch for coordination between facilities and emergency management on tanker use and connection specs.
